draft.title: Sympathetic and parasympathetic
card: The autonomic nervous system has two branches. They work as a pair and often have opposite effects on the same organ.
readies the body for action. It raises heart rate and breathing rate, and it is most active when a person faces a threat or is under stress.
calms the body and keeps it steady. It slows heart rate and breathing, and it helps the body return to its resting state after a threat has passed.
Both branches are active at the same time. Which one has more influence at a given moment depends on what the body needs.
draft.remember: Sympathetic gets the body ready for action. Parasympathetic settles it and keeps it steady.

a.q: Which change would the sympathetic nervous system produce?
opts: A faster heart rate and faster breathing
A slower heart rate and slower breathing
A steady heart rate while at rest
A return to normal breathing after a threat
a.why: The sympathetic branch readies the body for action, so heart rate and breathing speed up. Slowing and settling the body is the work of the parasympathetic branch, so the other options describe that branch.
a.clue: Think about what the body needs to do when facing a threat.

b.q: Priya has just finished a nervous speech in front of her class and sits down. Over the next few minutes her heart rate and breathing return to normal. Which branch is having more influence?
opts: The parasympathetic branch, which calms the body
The sympathetic branch, which readies the body
The somatic system, which controls her movements
The sympathetic branch, which keeps the body steady
b.why: Her body is settling back to its resting state after stress, which is the job of the parasympathetic branch. The sympathetic branch is tempting because the speech was stressful, but it raises arousal and does not calm the body.
b.clue: Is her body getting ready for action, or settling down?

a.best: A faster heart rate and faster breathing

b.best: The parasympathetic branch, which calms the body
